title: Global units modulo relatively integrally closed constants are finitely generated
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X$ be a nonempty connected reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme] locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that $X$ has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and assume the induced map identifies $k$ with a subfield of $A$ which is integrally closed in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $A^\times/k^\times$ is a finitely generated abelian group: there are finitely many units whose classes generate the quotient. Here $A^\times$ is the multiplicative group of invertible elements of $A$, and $k^\times$ is its subgroup of nonzero constants.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K/k$. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-connected-component-surjective] to $X$: choose a nonempty connected component $Y$ of $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$. It is reduced and locally of finite type over $K$, has finitely many irreducible components, and its map $p:Y\to X$ is surjective. Put $B=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ and let $\alpha:A\to B$ be pullback of functions.

source.place: Tag 04L7 (proposition-units-general), first paragraph, choice of Y and finiteness of its components.

proof.text: The map $\alpha$ is injective. Indeed if $\alpha(a)=0$, for each $x\in X$ choose $y\in Y$ over $x$. The field map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is injective, so $a(x)=0$. For any reduced scheme $W$, clauses (1) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], applied to the whole closed subset $|W|$ and the identity immersion of $W$, say that the ideal sheaf of sections vanishing in every residue field is zero. Thus $a=0$ on $X$. The same criterion will detect equality of sections on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 04L7 (proposition-units-general), justification of the injection of global functions from reducedness and surjectivity; Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme).

proof.text: Let $Y_i$, for $i$ in a finite nonempty set $I$, be the irreducible components of $Y$ with their reduced induced closed-subscheme structures, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each is integral. It is locally of finite type over $K$: on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Y$ with $R$ finitely generated over $K$, the closed subscheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak p_i)$, whose algebra generators are the images of those of $R$. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-units-finite-valuation-map] to obtain finite sets $J_i$ and homomorphisms $v_i:\Gamma(Y_i,\mathcal O_{Y_i})^\times\to\mathbf Z^{J_i}$ with kernel $K^\times$. The disjoint union $J=\coprod_iJ_i$ is finite. Define $w:B^\times\to\mathbf Z^J$ by restricting to $Y_i$ and applying $v_i$ in its coordinates.

source.place: Tag 04L6 (lemma-units-general-algebraically-closed), component restriction map, with Tag 04L5/04L4 supplying finite integer coordinates.

proof.text: The kernel of $w$ is exactly $K^\times$. If $w(b)=0$, then $b|_{Y_i}=c_i\in K^\times$. For $Y_i\cap Y_h\ne\varnothing$, evaluation at a point of the intersection gives $c_i=c_h$, since $K$ embeds in its residue field. The intersection graph of the finite closed cover $(Y_i)$ is connected: otherwise the unions indexed by a graph component and its complement are disjoint nonempty closed subsets covering $Y$, hence both open, contrary to connectedness. Consequently all $c_i$ equal one $c\in K^\times$. The section $b-c$ vanishes in every residue field of $Y$, so it is zero by step 2. Conversely constants are killed by each $v_i$.

source.place: Tag 04L6 (lemma-units-general-algebraically-closed), equality of constants on intersecting components and connectedness argument.

proof.text: Compose $w$ with $\alpha$ on units, obtaining $h:A^\times\to\mathbf Z^J$. If $h(u)=0$, step 4 gives $\alpha(u)=\lambda\in K^\times$. Since $K/k$ is algebraic, choose a nonzero polynomial over $k$ vanishing at $\lambda$ and divide by its nonzero leading coefficient to obtain a monic polynomial $P\in k[T]$. Compatibility of $\alpha$ with the scalar maps and polynomial evaluation gives $\alpha(P(u))=P(\lambda)=0$. Step 2 yields $P(u)=0$ in $A$. Relative integral closedness forces $u\in k$; because $u$ is a unit, this is a nonzero constant. Conversely $h$ kills $k^\times$. Hence $[u]\mapsto h(u)$ is a well-defined injection $A^\times/k^\times\hookrightarrow\mathbf Z^J$. By [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] this quotient is free of finite rank, in particular finitely generated. Representatives in $A^\times$ of a finite basis give the requested finitely many units.

source.place: Tag 04L7 (proposition-units-general), first paragraph, descent of a geometric scalar using alternative (1); finite free subgroup conclusion made explicit.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04L7 (proposition-units-general), alternative (1), using the component argument of Tag 04L6 (lemma-units-general-algebraically-closed). The finite integer coordinates from the proofs of 04L5 and 04L4 replace the intermediate abstract finite-generation argument.
